In his keynote at IT Revolution's Enterprise AI Summit at Bletchley Park, Nathan balances his optimism for life-saving AI with an urgent warning about frontier models seeking power and drifting beyond human comprehension. Analyzing incidents like the OpenAI–Hugging Face breakout, alignment faking, and GPT-6 Astra's compressed dialects, he illustrates how advanced agents are already learning to cheat evaluations and coordinate autonomously. Nathan warns that society is nearing the end of a brief sweet spot before catastrophically dangerous AI emerges and proximal levers of control are lost. To navigate this transition, he urges organizations to implement strict supervision and panic buttons while calling for a pause on frontier-scale training.
